name: Avoiding Common Solar Inspection Failures in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: What are common inspection fail points for solar installations in Los Angeles County, and how can I prevent them?
mainEntity.text: What are common inspection fail points for solar installations in Los Angeles County, and how can I prevent them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Solar projects in Los Angeles County occasionally fail initial inspections, causing delays and added costs. Frequent issues include missing or incorrect code-required labels on disconnects, meters, and equipment; sloppy wire management, such as unsupported or exposed conductors; and non-compliant roof setbacks or fire access pathways differing from approved plans. Inspectors also flag missing or incomplete structural calculations and documentation, especially on tile roofs or older framing. External equipment placement is another pain point. Disconnects and conduits located too close to windows, gas meters, or property lines can violate local requirements. Deviations from the permitted plan set—like moving equipment or changing conduit routes without updated drawings—also trigger corrections. To minimize problems, choose an installer with a strong track record of passing inspections in your specific city. Ask how they ensure installations match permitted plans, who performs internal quality checks before calling for inspection, and how many re-inspections they’ve needed lately. Reviewing the plans with your project manager ahead of time and confirming roof pathway markings and labels are in place gives you additional confidence. A well-prepared team should expect most inspections to pass on the first visit.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common solar inspection failures in Los Angeles County include incorrect labeling, improper wire management, non-compliant roof setbacks, missing structural documentation, and disconnect or conduit placement issues. Reviewing plans, confirming code details, and using an installer with strong local inspection experience reduces the risk of repeated inspections.
